facts: The paper 'Technofascism: AI, Big Tech, and the new authoritarianism' is authored by Mark Coeckelbergh.
The paper was published in the journal AI & SOCIETY on January 25, 2026 (DOI: 10.1007/s00146-026-02862-9).
It addresses how rapid digital technologies, including AI, introduce mechanisms of control, forms of organization, and ideological patterns resembling historical fascist phenomena.
It identifies an intersection between tech transformations and a broader Western political context of fascism, populism, authoritarianism, and illiberalism.
The paper's theoretical framework draws from classic philosophical and political theory literature on fascism, authoritarianism, and totalitarianism.
The core argument is that features of contemporary digital technologies, their governance, and their political environment mirror features of fascism.
The paper concludes with a call to resist these anti-democratic governance models and enact systemic changes to technology development and societal governance.
